title: Bonds payable life cycle — Harbor Freight Lines
instructions: On January 1, Year 1, Harbor Freight Lines issued **$2,000,000** of 5-year, **6%** bonds with interest paid **semiannually** on June 30 and December 31, when the market rate was **8%**. Use the effective interest method and round each amount to the nearest dollar.

exhibits.title: Present value factors (4% per period, 10 periods)
exhibits.content:
| Factor | Value |
|---|---:|
| PV of $1 | 0.67556 |
| PV of an ordinary annuity of $1 | 8.11090 |

exhibits.title: Year 3 event
exhibits.content: On **January 1, Year 3** (immediately after the December 31, Year 2 payment), Harbor repurchased **half** of the bonds in the open market at **97**.

parts.prompt: Compute the issue price and the first-year amortization.

rows.label: Issue price
rows.explanation: PV of face 2,000,000 × 0.67556 = 1,351,120; PV of coupons 60,000 × 8.11090 = 486,654; total ≈ **1,837,782** (rounding in factors may differ by a few dollars).

parts.prompt: Record the June 30, Year 1 interest payment.
parts.explanation: Cash = 2,000,000 × 3% = 60,000. Expense 73,511. The 13,511 difference amortizes (reduces) the discount.

parts.prompt: The January 1, Year 3 repurchase. The carrying amount of all the bonds on that date is $1,895,157.

rows.label: Carrying amount of the bonds repurchased
Gain (loss) on extinguishment — enter a loss as negative
rows.explanation: 947,579 − 970,000 = **(22,421)** loss, reported in income from continuing operations. Even though the price was below face, it was above the carrying amount.
